articles.title: Can Red Bull keep up their momentum after Verstappen's Sepang win?
articles.description: Max Verstappen's been in immense form all year – and Sepang win proved he now has a car to match, says former Renault F1 driver Jolyon Palmer.
articles.image_alt: KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Race winner Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red
body: Max Verstappen finally netted a 2026 victory with a dominant drive in Sepang. With the way that he's been driving this year it seemed inevitable that the Dutchman would hit the top step at some point this season, but I didn't expect it to come in as dominant fashion as we eventually saw.

Max had such a stranglehold on Qualifying, topping each part of it before posting two laps good enough for pole. His dominance on Saturday was enough that some of his nearest competitors at the front expected him to runaway and hide in the Grand Prix.
This performance begs the question: where has Red Bull's pace come from?

articles.title: What time is the 2026 Singapore GP and how can I watch it?
articles.description: Here are all the timings – along with all the additional information you need – for the 17th Grand Prix weekend of the 2026 season from Singapore.
articles.image_alt: SINGAPORE, SINGAPORE - OCTOBER 05: George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG
body: Here are all the timings – along with all the additional information you need – for the 17th Grand Prix weekend of the 2026 season from Singapore.

Formula 1 moves onto Singapore for the final stop in a triple header, with the Marina Bay Street Circuit set to host Round 17 of the 2026 season – and here are the global start times for Sunday's race.

George Russell's title hopes suffered another blow as he retired from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, enabling team mate Kimi Antonelli to extend his lead in the drivers' standings to a commanding 84 points. But even he couldn't match Max Verstappen, who clinched victory for the first time this year – will he be able to repeat the feat in Singapore, or will Antonelli return to the top?
Head to the RACE HUB or scroll down for more on how and when you can watch the action, along with the global start times for each session.

Singapore will hold the final Sprint of the season, which means drivers will only have one hour of Free Practice to find their rhythm at the track. That will begin at 1630 local time on Friday, 9 October before Sprint Qualifying follows at 2030.
The Sprint gets underway at 1700 on Saturday, 10 October ahead of Qualifying under the lights at 2100, while the Grand Prix itself takes place at 2000 on Sunday, 11 October.
Check out the image below to find all the global start times for Sunday's race.

You can enjoy coverage from every session live on F1 TV Pro (available in selected countries), which brings fans closer to the action via exclusive features like onboard cameras on all 22 of the drivers' cars, and access to both Pre-Race and Post-Race Shows.

F1 TV Pro can be streamed easily via Apple TV, Chromecast Generation 2 and above, Android TV, Google TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Roku. F1 TV Pro is free of ad breaks and available with commentary in six languages.

Fans can also watch via F1 TV Premium, a premier service that invites fans to step into the heart of the action with the ability to watch races in 4K Ultra HD/HDR on up to six different devices, as well as a personalised Multiview feature available on select devices with 26 different feeds to choose from.

Viewers can watch every F1 Grand Prix, F1 Sprint, Qualifying and practice session live in 4K Ultra HD/HDR at home, with F2, F3, F1 ACADEMY and Porsche Supercup sessions also available to watch live on the platform.
Alternatively, live timing will be available on F1.com and the F1 app across every session during the Grand Prix weekend.
Since making its debut in 2008, the Marina Bay Street Circuit has hosted every edition of the Singapore Grand Prix and delivered some of the most dramatic street races in recent memory.

The bulk of the action takes place at night against the stunning backdrop of the city skyline, but the temperatures and humidity barely go down despite the timing, making it one of the most physically demanding events of the season.
It's been the site of both heartbreak and triumph, with Sebastian Vettel winning a record five times between 2011 and 2019.

Conditions are currently expected to be very warm and humid, with temperatures reaching 32 Celsius. There's a chance of rain across Friday and Saturday which could impact driving conditions, but no precipitation is forecast for Sunday's Grand Prix.

articles.title: Who impressed our judges at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia?
articles.description: Max Verstappen delivered a masterclass as he and Red Bull returned to winning ways at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. But who else impressed our Power Rankings judges at the Sepang International Circuit? Check out the latest scores and overall leaderboard below...
body: Find out who topped the Power Rankings table after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Max Verstappen delivered a masterclass as he and Red Bull returned to winning ways at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. But who else impressed our Power Rankings judges at the Sepang International Circuit? Check out the latest scores and overall leaderboard below...

Verstappen, Red Bull and their all-new power unit have scored a solid number of podiums over the first 15 rounds of the season, but pole position and victory had eluded them. That was until last weekend at Sepang, where the Dutchman – making good use of recent updates – stormed his way to P1 on the grid and then mastered the mixed conditions on Sunday to bag a breakthrough win. Our judges were unanimous in giving him 10/10 scores.

Aston Martin and Honda's 2026 problems have been very well documented, but the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia marked a big step in the right direction for the new partnership. After securing a best grid slot of the campaign so far in P12, Fernando Alonso used all of his experience on a wet/dry race day to come away with a superb P8 finish.

It looked like it had all gone wrong for Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari at the start of Sunday's race, with P2 on the grid becoming P17 at the end of the first racing lap after a gamble to start on slick tyres backfired. However, the seven-time World Champion came back fighting as the track dried out, displaying rapid pace and pulling off a series of fine moves – passing Isack Hadjar for the final podium spot in the closing stages.

While Hamilton tumbled down the order on the first lap, intermediate-shod Liam Lawson charged his way from 11th to fourth. He enjoyed wheel-to-wheel moments with Verstappen's Red Bull, before understandably losing touch with the front-runners as conditions moved from damp to dry. Still, seventh place marked a great reward, and another boost for Racing Bulls in their battle for P5 in the standings with Alpine.

Mercedes faced a headache at Sepang as they tried to understand a host of car updates on a hot, demanding track surface. Kimi Antonelli salvaged fourth in Qualifying, which became third thanks to Hadjar's engine-related penalty, before charging into the lead at the start and then settling for second behind Verstappen. The personal struggles of Azerbaijan behind him, Antonelli was already set to gain points over George Russell when his team mate ground to a halt late on – boosting the Italian's championship lead to 84 points.

Hadjar impressed plenty of paddock figures when he returned to action from a wrist injury on the streets of Baku and bagged a podium finish. His strong form continued over the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia weekend, bringing third in Qualifying (before his penalty) and the potential for another rostrum in the tricky, wet/dry conditions. A slight drop in pace over the second half of the race allowed the two Ferraris through, but fifth still represented a very solid result.

Arvid Lindblad faced a massive recovery drive at Sepang after taking on new power unit elements and dropping to the very back of the grid. Remarkably, the Racing Bulls rookie made up 13 places on the first racing lap alone, putting him firmly in the mix for a points finish. After the transition from intermediates to slicks, Safety Cars, race restarts and more, a late move on Nico Hulkenberg earned himself and Racing Bulls another important point.

Speaking of Hulkenberg, the German had done plenty of things right on Sunday to rise from 15th on the grid to the points-paying positions. Unfortunately for the Audi driver, who has narrowly missed out on a reward plenty of times this season, Lindblad and McLaren's Lando Norris – after his off-track excursion behind the Safety Car – both managed to sneak past in the closing laps and deny him.

Esteban Ocon announced that he will be leaving Haas at the end of the 2026 season in the build-up to last weekend's event. Starting 17th, just behind team mate Ollie Bearman, he was another driver to make a sensational start to the race, climbing all the way to P7 and remaining in the top 10 over the first half. His and the team's pace faded as conditions got drier, but the Frenchman offered another glimpse of what he can do.

Carlos Sainz also made up a hatful of positions on the first racing lap, turning 13th (after another Q2 appearance) into sixth. He remained in the battle for points as the race developed, only to be tipped into a spin by Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto exiting Turn 2. Given the drying conditions, that effectively ended his chances of scoring points there and then.

Just missing out on the top 10 of this week's Power Rankings list are Lance Stroll, who also displayed encouraging pace for Aston Martin, as well as McLaren driver Oscar Piastri (who finished P6) and the aforementioned Russell (who had been on course for a podium).

articles.title: Why didn't Mercedes' upgrades provide a boost in Malaysia?
articles.description: Mark Hughes and Giorgio Piola delve into the upgrade package Mercedes introduced at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
articles.image_alt: KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG
body: Mercedes' first big upgrade since the Canadian Grand Prix over three months ago did not bring the hoped-for boost in performance around Sepang and the team are currently deep-diving into the data to understand why.

The specification change was targeted at improving medium-high speed downforce, where the car had fallen steadily further behind its rivals in recent races. To achieve this aim, the whole mass of the bodywork has been brought forwards to create more free volume ahead of the rear wheels. This has entailed moving the cooling channels to create ‘cannons' between the sidepods and engine cover.

articles.title: How an unexpected battle for P6 in Malaysia fell apart
articles.description: Williams and Haas had a rare opportunity to challenge for higher points in the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but ultimately came away with nothing.
articles.image_alt: KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Thirteenth placed qualifier Carlos Sainz of Spain and Williams
body: Williams and Haas had a rare opportunity to challenge for higher points in the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but ultimately came away with nothing.
Formula 1's midfield is so closely matched that points are hard to come by, and any top-10 finish counts as a real achievement.
So when factors such as rain throw a curve ball and create opportunities, it's essential for those teams and their drivers to get everything right and take full advantage.

For Carlos Sainz, Alex Albon and Esteban Ocon the early stages of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia promised much as they made the right tyre calls and did the job on track to charge into the top eight. However, in the end, all three were to be left disappointed.

Ocon was one of the drivers who hit problems at the original start attempt, but having been given a second chance he and Haas got it right by opting for intermediates for the start as the team split its two cars. Williams also made the optimum call by putting both drivers on inters.

On the first lap it was almost like a video game for all three, as they picked their way past those ahead who had started on slicks. At the end of the lap Sainz was P6 (from 13th), Albon P7 (from 18th) and Ocon P8 (from 17th). The Haas driver was flying, and he soon made his way past both FW48s to claim P6.
At that stage – and with the slick runners falling far behind – it was looking good for all three, but the fun was not to last.
Albon was running behind Sainz when the first Safety Car sent the field into the pits for slicks, and he lost places while double-stacked behind his team mate.

At the restart Sainz was nudged into a spin at Turn 2 by Gabriel Bortoleto. With faster cars that started on slicks gaining ground under the Safety Car both Williams drivers tumbled down the order, with Albon also fighting brake problems. Sainz had to settle for P17 at the flag.

“We were having the race and doing everything right to score a point or two today,” said the Spaniard. “But then the race went away from us, obviously with the touch with Gabi taking us off. Even though I left the space, I don't think he expected the inside of Turn 2 to be wet, and he just bumped into me.
“It was dry from there on, and it's not like our pace was amazing. Our pit stops were also not good. So it would have been a difficult day anyway.

“We would have needed to execute a perfect race, and we had two very slow pit stops. And the execution of the race from there onwards wasn't great either. I don't know if that bump from Gabi threw us off a bit as a team, but from there it was a bit scrappy, to be honest.”
To add insult to injury, Albon didn't even see the flag due to a late gearbox problem.

“I lost out on the double stack,” he said. “We had to box early because I flat-spotted my soft tyres with the brake issue. So then it just felt like it fell away from us. The performance was nowhere, but also nowhere on my side as well.

“Unfortunately, you just want a smooth weekend, a feeling of progress, but we've had issues with parts this weekend. Not lack of parts, just performing parts, and unfortunately, if you're not on the one part that you have, you use your second best stuff, it's not good enough, and you're immediately on the back foot. And I was on the back foot massively all weekend.”
In contrast to the two Williams drivers, Ocon survived the first Safety Car period in good shape, and still in P6.
He lost a place to the flying Lewis Hamilton, but was still P7 when he made a relatively early second stop.
Others who hung on for a later stop benefited from the second Safety Car, triggered by Albon. Points thus slipped out of his hands, and he finished P15.

“We took the right tyre for the start, I decided to stay on the inter, which was the right thing,” said the Frenchman. “We had a mega first lap on the inter, I was overtaking cars. I was up to P6. It was really good. And then from the first time we boxed, we started moving rearwards.
“So we need to exactly see what happened, but we deserved more today. We had new tyres in stock. We also boxed to used tyres at the end, and we missed the last Safety Car also.

“So 100% the start of the race, 0% at the end part of the race, of success. A bit of mixed emotion, but super sad for the whole team that has worked super hard to get this car to where it was, because it was healthy, it was working well.

“We had great pace on the soft tyre in the beginning and on the inter, and we should have been fighting for the points, and we were there. So very disappointed. But it's our fault – so we'll keep working on it.”

articles.title: Audi unpick eventful weekend amid penalty and last-lap drama
articles.description: Nico Hulkenberg narrowly missed out on scoring a point for Audi at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while team mate Gabriel Bortoleto saw his race unfold following a collision with Carlos Sainz.
body: Nico Hulkenberg narrowly missed out on scoring a point for Audi at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while team mate Gabriel Bortoleto saw his race unfold following a collision with Carlos Sainz.

The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia proved to be a particularly eventful weekend for Audi, with the squad left to reflect on a “frustrating” end to Sunday's race that saw them lose out on points during the last lap.

After progressing to Q3 in Saturday's Qualifying, Gabriel Bortoleto lined up in P10 on the grid while team mate Nico Hulkenberg started from P15 – but both looked set for a tough start to the race when they bolted on soft tyres, a decision that quickly went against them given the still damp conditions from the heavy rainfall that had delayed the event getting underway.

Following an early stop for the intermediates, the Audis were each able to make gains. However, Bortoleto's progress faltered when he made contact with the Williams of Carlos Sainz, an incident that the Brazilian subsequently received a 10-second time penalty for.

Hulkenberg, meanwhile, remained in the fight for points until the very end of the race and only just missed out after being overtaken by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad on the final lap of the Grand Prix.

Furthermore, the team were handed a fine (part of which was suspended for 12 months on the condition that there is not a similar incident in that time) for an unsafe release of Hulkenberg during a pit stop.
While he had also seen a point slip away during the final stages of the race one week earlier in Azerbaijan, Hulkenberg was pragmatic about experiencing a similar fate at Sepang.

“Obviously a few times now I just missed out, but ultimately [it was] not quite good enough, our package here,” the German explained. “That's why we couldn't hang on to that point in the end, but obviously if we're honest we only got there because of some retirements and some trouble at the front.

“I feel like it was always a long shot, but I'm much happier with my performance compared to yesterday, which wasn't so difficult, but a clean race from my side. Yeah, good racing and a good afternoon.”
On the other side of the garage, Bortoleto took the blame for his collision with Sainz after what proved to be a tough afternoon in Malaysia.

“First I want to apologise to Carlos,” said Bortoleto. “I ended up touching him there and maybe destroyed his race, a bit of mine as well, created damage in my car, and after that we were just too far behind to fight for anything.

“I was racing on my own and unfortunately had another few issues through the race as well that was very difficult to manage, but anyway, I was already gone after my contact. So I apologise to him, to my team, to his team, and we move to Singapore.“

The 21-year-old still felt that there were “a lot of positives” to take forward, adding: “I think we delivered a good upgrade in Baku and it showed to be strong here. And yeah, heads up to Singapore. I'm excited for the weekend, and hopefully we can have a good one there.”
Audi's Racing Director Allan McNish echoed that positivity, having praised the performance of the car in Malaysia whilst acknowledging that missing out on points was a frustrating end to the event.

“We got the pace of the car. That was quite clear when we got to Qualifying,” McNish reflected after the race. “I think we had got it into the right window, and Gabi delivered a really good Qualifying.
“Nico was on a similar pace till Turn 14. These things happen. And I think, we sort of got back through to roughly that point by the end of the race. Not quite that same point, but very close to it.

“So in terms of that, yeah, it was a bit frustrating to be overtaken in the last lap again, because that's two races consecutively where we've been done in the last lap and that's a little bit frustrating. But I think we know where our strengths and weaknesses are and we know we're a bit exposed, and when the Safety Car came out we become a bit more exposed.”
